newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND TRIUMPH FAILS TO IMPRESS BAYERN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND TRIUMPH FAILS TO IMPRESS BAYERN.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund's surprise 1-0 victory at Atletico Madrid in the Champions' League on Wednesday has given the injury-hit German club a huge shot-in-the-arm before Sunday's crunch Bundesliga clash with Bayern Munich.
But the record champions are not impressed. Many Bayern players did not even bother to watch the match on television.

"A team that wins in Madrid can also win in Munich with the same kind of performance," Dortmund captain Michael Zorc said on Thursday after Stefan Reuter had celebrated his 30th birthday with one of the most important goals of his career in the Spanish capital.
Coach Ottmar Hitzfeld added: "It's sensational. You can't speak highly enough of this win."
The victory effectively secured the 1995 and 1996 Bundesliga champions a place in the quarter-finals of the European Cup with three wins in as many games in Group B.

Bayern chairman Franz Beckenbauer was forced to watch the victory since he works as a television pundit for the channel which broadcast the game live. But many of his players did not take the time to do a little homework on their opponents.
"I'm sorry. I didn't see it," Bayern striker Juergen Klinsmann admitted.
Midfield playmaker Mehmet Scholl prefered to celebrate his 26th birthday with a dinner with friends. Defender Markus Babbel just watched the first-half.
The victory provided a huge lift to Hitzfeld's team after they have struggled to be consistent in the German first division following an array of injuries to key players.
After 10 games, Dortmund are fourth in the table, four points behind record champions Bayern who moved level on points with leaders VfB Stuttgart last weekend.

A victory on Sunday evening in front of a capacity 63,000 crowd in Munich's Olympic stadium would put Dortmund back on course on the domestic scene and help quash rumours the club is suffering from internal squabbles.
"People on the outside have tried to create problems within the team," veteran German international defender Juergen Kohler said.
"Let's get it clear. There are no arguments and no cliques, otherwise a performance like this would not have been possible. Every player was ready to do each other's dirty work on the pitch."

Dortmund will again be without their key libero Matthias Sammer against Bayern but there were reports in Dortmund on Thursday that playmaker Andy Moeller may be fit enough to return after a pulled leg muscle.

Bayern learned on Thursday that Babbel and midfielder Markus Muench, both confined to bed on Wednesday because of flu, would be fit to play. Midfielder Thomas Strunz is also keen to return after recovering from a back problem.

The Bavarians, however, will be without international wing-back Christian Ziege and defender Thomas Helmer who both have long-term injuries. There is also a doubt about creative midfielder Mario Basler who has a leg muscle problem.
Manager Uli Hoeness, though, refuses to risk anyone who is not 100 per cent fit as the Bavarians prepare to defend their unbeaten run at home this season.
"We are always saying we have 18 players of equal quality," Hoeness said. "As long as we have 12 fit players there is no reason to complain."
